plans.headline: Discovery Drop-In, Storytime and Meet the Keepers at Sarah P. Duke Gardens

main.why: Sarah P. Duke Gardens hosts a free drop-in discovery program with themed activities and two storytimes, then Meet the Keepers gives a close-up look at the garden's bees, chickens and edible plants. Both are fully outdoors and free.
tips: Pack a picnic lunch to eat in the gardens before Meet the Keepers begins at 13:00.
The 10:30 and 11:30 storytimes are in the Charlotte Brody Discovery Garden; head there first.
Leave by 13:50 to get home in time for the second nap.

alternatives.why: The fall festival at Hill Ridge Farms lets toddlers roam a working farm with animals and open fields. Each gate ticket includes a free pumpkin.
tips: Last admission is one hour before closing; plan to arrive well before 13:00.
Pack extra layers — farm mornings in November can be cool.
Leave by 13:00 to get home in time for the afternoon nap.

alternatives.why: A self-guided StoryWalk along the accessible loop at Beech Bluff County Park weaves a picture book through the trail — a calm, free outdoor morning good for any pace.
tips: The walk is self-paced and drop-in; great for a toddler who likes to stop and look at things.
Pair with play in the park area before heading back.
Leave by 13:45 to get home before the afternoon nap.

alternatives.why: A short live science program at the NC Museum of Natural Sciences gives a focused, engaging window for curious toddlers in the afternoon slot.
tips: The program runs 30 minutes; arrive a few minutes early to find a good spot.
Leave right at 14:00 to be home before the second nap.
A small snack in the car helps the transition home.

tips: No registration needed; drop in from 10:50.
Good for a toddler who likes stacking and pulling things apart.
Leave by 13:30 to get home for a quick lunch before the second nap.

plans.headline: Crawl through tunnels and shake a parachute in the gym

main.why: Your toddler can crawl through tunnels and play with a parachute in the gym at Total Tot Time, alongside other little ones. A family needs to sign up first.
tips: Sign up before you go, since this program needs a spot.
Let your child pick between the tunnel and the parachute and follow their lead.
Bring a water bottle and a snack for the ride home, then lunch before the 2:30 pm nap.

alternatives.why: This is a drop-in maker table at Durham Main Library where your child can stack, pull and build with cardboard and Makedo kits at their own pace.
tips: Drop in any time and stay as long as it holds their interest.
Offer big, simple pieces and let them explore first.
Pack a snack for the car.
